benchmarks.label: Top education approaches (~3 LAYS per $100), Angrist et al. 2020
benchmarks.source_title: How to Improve Education Outcomes Most Efficiently? A Comparison of 150 Interventions Using the New Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling Metric (CGD Working Paper 558)
benchmarks.publisher: Center for Global Development (also World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 9450)
benchmarks.quote: some policies that improve the productivity of each year of schooling, such as targeting instruction to a child's learning level or structured lesson plans, can yield on average of around 3 additional LAYS per $100.
benchmarks.notes: Source states ~3 LAYS per $100 for the best approaches (targeted instruction, structured lesson plans). Stored as inputs $100 / 3 LAYS; the app's calculator computes cost per LAYS. 'around 3' is approximate and is an average of top-performing categories, so this is a demanding bar.

benchmarks.label: GEEAP 2023 'Smart Buys' report
benchmarks.source_title: 2023 Cost-Effective Approaches to Improve Global Learning: What does recent evidence tell us are 'Smart Buys' for improving learning in low- and middle-income countries?
benchmarks.publisher: Global Education Evidence Advisory Panel (World Bank, FCDO, UNICEF, USAID)
benchmarks.quote: In Angrist et al (2020), the preferred metric for cost-effectiveness is LAYS per $100; this measures how many years of high-quality schooling can be gained for an additional $100 spent on each intervention
benchmarks.notes: The report rates interventions qualitatively (Great Buys / Good Buys / Bad Buys) and shows LAYS per $100 (2015 USD) only in a log-scale box-plot figure (Appendix E, Figure 1); no numeric LAYS-per-$100 benchmark appears in the text, so no value recorded. Date 2023-05 from the World Bank press release of May 9, 2023 announcing the report. Full PDF (35 MB) downloaded with curl and text-searched.

benchmarks.label: US EPA social cost of carbon (2020 emissions, 2% discount)
benchmarks.source_title: Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases: Estimates Incorporating Recent Scientific Advances
benchmarks.publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (National Center for Environmental Economics; Climate Change Division)
benchmarks.quote: Table ES.1 ... (2020 dollars per metric ton of CO2) ... Near-term rate 2.5% 2.0% 1.5% ... 2020 120 190 340
benchmarks.notes: Quote is assembled from cells of Table ES.1 (text extracted from the fetched PDF); the 190 figure appears only in the table, not in prose. 2020 dollars; SC-CO2 for emissions in year 2020 at the 2.0% near-term Ramsey discount rate (EPA's central rate); rounded to two significant figures. Rises to 230 for 2030 emissions. This is a damage (social cost) value, not an abatement cost. Report cover dated November 2023 (posted under a 2023-12 URL path). The EPA SC-GHG web page (https://www.epa.gov/environmental-economics/scghg) returned HTTP 404 on the access date, so the policy status of this estimate may have changed; the PDF itself was still retrievable. RFF commentary (Feb 13, 2023) independently states the same '$190 per tonne CO2' central estimate for 2020.

benchmarks.label: Founders Pledge: top climate charities avert a tonne for < $10
benchmarks.quote: have in the past averted a tonne of CO2 for less than $10 in expectation
benchmarks.notes: This is an UPPER BOUND ('less than $10'), not a point estimate; it is used here as a threshold/bar for 'highly cost-effective' climate giving. Expected-value estimate for leveraged advocacy charities (CATF, Coalition for Rainforest Nations at the time); highly speculative. Date is the page's 'updated' date. The same page calls offsets promising 'a tonne of CO2 with high confidence for $1 or less' unrealistic.

benchmarks.label: Average voluntary carbon credit price (Ecosystem Marketplace)
benchmarks.source_title: SOVCM 2025 Finds the Voluntary Carbon Market in Transition: Demand Holding Steady as Turnover Stabilizes
benchmarks.quote: credit prices declined by only 5.5 percent
benchmarks.notes: Could not confirm a dollar average price per tonne from a primary fetched source. Fetched the SOVCM 2025 press article and the 2024 and 2025 SOVCM publication pages: none state a $/t figure in fetchable text (full reports appear gated). Secondary sources (Statista, CarbonCredits.com, a Farmonaut blog) cite figures like $7.37/t (2022) or $6.37/t (US, 2024) but these were not verified against Ecosystem Marketplace and are not used.

charities.name: Youth Impact (ConnectEd phone tutoring)
charities.program: Low-tech phone call + SMS math tutoring (ConnectEd); figure from the IPA-supported Philippines scale-up/replication
charities.source_title: Building Resilient Education Systems: Cost-effective Mobile Tutoring in the Philippines and Beyond
charities.quote: The program has an average cost of approximately $12 per child ... yielding 3.4 learning-adjusted years of schooling (LAYS) per $100 spent
charities.notes: Stated directly as LAYS per $100 (recorded as cost 100, outcome 3.4). No publication date shown on the page (study timeline 2021-2022; project brief file path dated 2023-05). Implementing partner context: the ConnectEd model originated with Youth Impact in Botswana; this specific estimate is from the Philippines evaluation. A search snippet of Youth Impact's own page reported 3.7 LAYS per $100, but that page (youth-impact.org/copy-of-connected) returned 404 so it could not be verified. Program-delivery costs only; dollar year not stated.

charities.name: CAMFED (Campaign for Female Education)
charities.program: Bursaries plus learning support (study guides, Learner Guide mentors) for marginalised girls in Tanzanian secondary schools
charities.source_title: Cost-effectiveness with equity: Raising learning for marginalised girls through Camfed's programme in Tanzania (Research and Policy Paper 18/2)
charities.publisher: REAL Centre, University of Cambridge (Sabates, Rose, Delprato, Alcott)
charities.quote: for all children supported through Camfed's programme, the cost-effectiveness analysis finds that the impact is equivalent to an extra 1.7 years of schooling per $100 spent.
charities.notes: Outcome is 'equivalent additional years of schooling' derived from English test-score gains (SD per $100 divided by one control-group year of learning, Romero-Sandefur-Sandholtz method) -- NOT LAYS, so not strictly comparable with LAYS figures. Quasi-experimental design; Camfed had funding/data role (acknowledged; funded by Echidna Giving). Equity-weighted version gives 2 years per $100; sustainability/scale scenarios 2.2-2.4. Costs at current values for 2013-2015, excluding school fees abolished in 2016.

charities.name: Evidence Action - Deworm the World Initiative (school-based deworming)
charities.program: Mass school-based deworming; schooling effect estimated from the Kenya Primary School Deworming Project
charities.publisher: J-PAL (Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab)
charities.quote: We estimate that school-based deworming adds 11.9 years of education per US$100 spent.
charities.notes: Outcome is additional years of school PARTICIPATION/attendance, not learning-adjusted years; deworming showed no clear test-score gains, so this is not comparable to LAYS (Angrist et al. 2020 by contrast report health interventions at 'up to 10 LAYS gains per $100'). Estimate is J-PAL's for the deworming intervention generally (Kenya, Miguel & Kremer), not an Evidence Action-specific cost-effectiveness figure. Page originally published Oct 2018, last updated Sept 2022. Cost cited as 'less than US$0.60 per child per year'. Dollar year not stated on page.

charities.name: Pratham (Teaching at the Right Level)
charities.program: Grouping children by learning level rather than grade for basic reading/math (TaRL), India
charities.source_title: How to Improve Education Outcomes Most Efficiently? A Comparison of 150 Interventions Using the New Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling Metric (CGD Working Paper 558)
charities.quote: In India, targeted instruction yields up to 4 additional learning-adjusted years of schooling per $100
charities.notes: Only an upper bound ('up to 4' LAYS per $100) for the targeted-instruction category in India was found in text; no central Pratham-specific estimate, so recorded as missing per the range rule. Per-intervention values exist only as unlabeled-in-text bar chart data (Figure 5) that could not be reliably matched to intervention names. J-PAL's TaRL page gives costs (often < $10 per child per year) and SD effects (0.07-0.70) but no years-of-schooling figure.

charities.name: Educate Girls
charities.program: Enrolment drives and remedial learning for girls in Rajasthan, India (incl. the 2015-2018 Development Impact Bond)
charities.source_title: World's First Education DIB | Educate Girls
charities.notes: No source found stating cost per learning-adjusted or additional year of schooling. The DIB page returned HTTP 503. Search results (Brookings, IDinsight final evaluation) give DIB budget ($270,000, ~7,300 children) and learning gains in test-score units and outcome payment prices, but not a years-of-schooling metric; converting would require my own assumptions, so not done.

charities.name: Conditional cash transfers (e.g., PROGRESA, Mexico)
charities.program: Cash payments conditional on school enrolment/attendance
charities.source_title: How to Improve Education Outcomes Most Efficiently? A Comparison of 150 Interventions Using the New Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling Metric (CGD Working Paper 558)
charities.quote: We find that cash transfers are not a costeffective tool to improve LAYS
charities.notes: Qualitative conclusion only: the text gives no numeric LAYS-per-$100 for CCTs (the Figure 5 bar chart lists 'ccts, MEX' among the lowest values but text extraction cannot reliably match values to labels). Recorded as missing; useful as a low-cost-effectiveness contrast. ('costeffective' is as it appears in the extracted PDF text.)

charities.name: Clean Air Task Force (CATF)
charities.program: Policy advocacy for neglected technologies (carbon capture, advanced nuclear, methane, etc.)
charities.source_title: A guide to the changing landscape of high-impact climate philanthropy
charities.quote: it makes sense to assume that the average project is 10x less cost-effective than this project, resulting in a cost of USD 1/tCO2e as a conservative guess.
charities.notes: Highly speculative, leveraged advocacy estimate. Derived from CATF's 45Q tax-credit work: $1.63/tonne US-domestic and ~$0.11/tonne global, then divided by 10 for an average project to give USD 1/tCO2e. Founders Pledge itself says 'this estimate will clearly be wrong' and is 'illustrative, not meant to be precise'. Text extracted from the fetched PDF.

charities.name: Evergreen Collaborative
charities.program: US climate policy development and advocacy (e.g., Clean Electricity Performance Program)
charities.source_title: Climate Recommendations in EA: Giving Green and Founders Pledge
charities.publisher: Giving Green (Kim Huynh, Dan Stein), posted on the Effective Altruism Forum
charities.quote: Evergreen Collaborative – $0.54 per metric ton of CO2e
charities.notes: Giving Green's expected-value estimate for policy advocacy; authors say 'The precise numbers should be considered rough estimates' and compare only at order-of-magnitude level. Posted by Giving Green on the EA Forum; the linked primary Giving Green deep-dive page (givinggreen.earth/us-policy-change-research/evergreen-collaborative%3A-deep-dive) returned 404 and archive.org was not reachable, so the figure is confirmed only via this Giving Green-authored post. Estimate dates from 2021; may be superseded.

charities.name: Carbon180
charities.program: US policy advocacy for carbon removal
charities.source_title: Climate Recommendations in EA: Giving Green and Founders Pledge
charities.publisher: Giving Green (Kim Huynh, Dan Stein), posted on the Effective Altruism Forum
charities.quote: Carbon180 – $0.66 per metric ton of CO2e
charities.notes: Giving Green's expected-value estimate for advocacy ('in expectation'); heavy uncertainty, rough order-of-magnitude only. Primary deep-dive page (givinggreen.earth/us-policy-change-research/carbon180%3A-deep-dive) returned 404; confirmed only via this Giving Green-authored post. Estimate from 2021; may be superseded.

charities.name: Cool Earth
charities.program: Partnering with rainforest communities to prevent deforestation
charities.quote: we estimate that Cool Earth is able to reduce emissions by 1 tonne of CO2-equivalent for every $1.34 donated
charities.notes: Old (2016) and marked by GWWC as superseded/historical; GWWC no longer does its own charity evaluations. Covers directly protected forest; $0.38/t if indirectly shielded forest included. Forest-protection estimates carry additionality/permanence/leakage uncertainty; EA Forum critiques consider it optimistic. Dollar year not stated.

charities.name: TerraPraxis
charities.program: Repowering coal plants with advanced heat sources; advanced nuclear advocacy
charities.notes: No published cost-per-tonne estimate found. Searches of Giving Green and Founders Pledge material returned no numeric figure for TerraPraxis (Founders Pledge grants to it but publishes qualitative rationale).
